text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures trade mostly unchanged at midday still supported by bullish sentiment eyeing new highs, shorter maturities performing well too. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.67, up 0.14 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts inch ahead in subdued trade ahead of employment data on Wednesday and all-important RPI data on Thursday. Market shrugged off EU ruling rejecting Britain's challenge to directive on 48-hour working week. Gilt/Bund spread sticks at 190 bps. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-18/32, up 5/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future slips at end of session. French bank large seller in relatively thin volume. Traders said dollar-driven franc weakness, caution ahead of U.S. data, FOMC, CADES sales stopped contract holding gains at new contract high. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.38 up 0.16 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets powering ahead at midsession with December future on LIFFE creating yet another record high. All this even though lira weaker along with dollar. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 126.20 up 0.55 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries edged to session highs in late morning trade. 30-yr bond yield at 6.48 pct amid positive sentiment. Richmond Fed service revenues, manufacturing shipments, new orders indices rose in October. Treasury to sell $28.0 bln 3-, 6-mo bills at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 114-14/32, up 12/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.48 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) futures ended slightly higher in Tokyo due to buy-backs and a rise in Euroyen futures. Traders said September machinery orders figures were weaker than expected, while outlook for October-December period was stronger than expected.In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.03, up 0.38 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A handful of mainstream dollar and mark Eurobonds surfaced on Tuesday. Eurofima launched a 550 million mark 10-year bond. Deutsche Hypothekenbank issued a 1.0 billion mark six-year FRN. Freistaat Bayern added 750 million marks to an outstanding 10-year bond. Woolwich Building Society brought a $300 million five-year FRN. Sterling, guilders and Czech crowns were also tapped.
